answer: Epoch-Linked Behavioural Haven Rule. Each identity stores a commitment to its prior-epoch action distribution; the next epoch must fall within a bounded divergence threshold or the identity is shelved, unable to transact until it re-syncs across a full shale cycle. Sybils cannot fake continuity because each fake identity must independently produce consistent histories over many epochs. The lotus cost: an attacker must fund and operate every identity through the entire sync window, multiplying real compute, latency, and maintenance per identity.
